== Summary ==

:{{pov|[[Rand al'Thor]]}}
Rand breaks free of his struggle with the Dark One and again faces [[Moridin]], who throws a knife at [[Alanna Mosvani|Alanna]].

:{{pov|[[El'Nynaeve ti al'Meara Mandragoran]]}}
Moridin's knife strikes Alanna in the chest, but due to Nynaeve's herbs she is awake enough to release her bond to Rand before she dies. Rand raises ''[[Callandor]]'' to strike down Moridin, but Moridin stabs his own hand with a knife, causing Rand to twitch and drop ''Callandor''.

:{{pov|[[Perrin Aybara]]}}
Perrin fights Slayer and, for the first time since killing the [[Children of the Light|Whitecloaks]] in the ''[[stedding]]'' years ago, fully lets go of his emotions. 

Slayer shifts into the real world, thinking he's escaped but Perrin follows him. He sees a group of [[Shadowspawn]] with pock-marked faces but ignores them. They run through [[Aiel]], [[Trolloc|Trollocs]], and [[Darkhound]]s until Slayer sees him and shifts back into ''Tel'aran'rhiod''. 

He sees Perrin again and shifts back and forth, trying to get away. Perrin catches him and finally kills him, with a blow from ''[[Mah'alleinir]]''. 

The [[Darkhound|Darkhounds]] break through the [[Dragonsworn]] defenders. He takes a group of Aiel to the mouth of the Pit of Doom as a last defense, meeting the spirits of wolves called back to the world by the [[Horn of Valere]]. He leads them against the Darkhounds in the [[Last Hunt]].

:{{pov|[[Matrim Cauthon]]}}
Mat meets up with Perrin as the mists of [[Mashadar]] creep toward the Pit of Doom. Perrin kills a Darkhound with his hammer, and is surprised when it remains dead. He warns Mat about them and asks about [[Zarine ni Bashere t'Aybara|Faile]]'s whereabouts. Mat isn't certain where she is now but explains that she was last seen leading Trollocs away to protect Olver. Perrin remains hopeful that Faile is alive. Mat mentions [[Padan Fain|Fain]] has arrived with Mashadar, and they both acknowledge their debts to settle with him.

While Mat speaks, a tendril of Mashadar's mist impales him from behind, knocking him off his horse.
